title: How to Export Securonix Logs
content_md: Generate an API token, run your Spotter query through the Securonix REST API (/ws/spotter/index/search), and save the events as JSON. When the source sent raw text, the original line is usually kept in the raw event field. Spotter in the UI can export results too. Securonix pulls in large volumes of activity data for UEBA and SIEM, which makes it a rich place to export an investigation slice from. Prime Core has 14,283 detection rules for Securonix, mapped to 620 MITRE ATT&CK techniques. Below is how to get data out, sanitize it, and investigate it for free in LogTotal. Get Started For Free Before you start API access. You need a Securonix user that’s allowed to use the API. Tokens are generated with that user’s credentials and have a validity period you choose. Your tenant URL. Cloud tenants usually look like https:// .securonix.net/Snypr. Retention. Hot data is searchable directly in Spotter. Older data may sit in long-term storage that needs extra steps to search. Export with the REST API BASE="https:// .securonix.net/Snypr" # 1. token, valid for one day TOKEN=$(curl -sS -H "username: $SNX_USER" -H "password: $SNX_PASS" -H "validity: 1" \ "$BASE/ws/token/generate") # 2. Spotter query for a time window curl -sS -G -H "token: $TOKEN" "$BASE/ws/spotter/index/search" \ --data-urlencode 'query=index=activity AND devicehostname="web-03"' \ --data-urlencode 'eventtime_from=10/19/2026 00:00:00' \ --data-urlencode 'eventtime_to=10/20/2026 00:00:00' \ > snx_web03_1019.json # 3. one
